gaps.construct: byte/rune literals such as '[' , '^', '/', '\\' compared with chunk[0] and s[0]
gaps.description: The doc has no character or byte literal and no conversion from a one-character Text to a byte; `byte "["` was invented.

gaps.construct: string slicing chunk = chunk[1:], s = s[n:], and returning the suffix s as rest
gaps.description: No slice or substring view exists. Re-slicing became two cursor variables, and the returned suffix is copied with a comprehension, which forces `uses memory` and OutOfMemory onto a function that allocates nothing in Go.

gaps.construct: switch on a byte value with case '[', case '?', case '\\' with fallthrough, default
gaps.description: `choose` is only shown for choice variants and maybe, and there is no fallthrough, so the switch became an if chain and the fallthrough was folded into the default branch.

gaps.construct: for { ... break } infinite loop parsing class ranges
gaps.description: Written as `repeat while true` plus `stop`; the required `decreases` line depends on an unstated property of getEsc (it always consumes input), which the original never documents.

gaps.construct: (rest string, ok bool, err error) results, and getEsc/DecodeRuneInString returning pairs
gaps.description: No tuples. The main result maps cleanly to maybe Bytes plus fails with BadPattern, but the helpers' pairs need ad hoc record types (Escape, DecodedRune).

gaps.construct: indexing a Go string yields a byte; Text vs Bytes
gaps.description: The doc never says what `item i of` returns for Bytes or Text, or what the element type is.
No escape rules for text literals are given.
The doc never shows boolean literals or a Bool type name.

gaps.construct: comprehension over an index range to build the suffix
gaps.description: Comprehensions are shown only over a list (`for each order in orders`); range comprehensions, their allocator and whether they need `try` are not specified.

notes: The Go code indexes chunk[0] after getEsc and s[0] in the '?' case without bounds checks, relying on getEsc's undocumented behaviour and on the earlier failed-check; a Scribe prover would need postconditions on get_esc that the original never states. The (rest, ok, err) result maps very naturally to `maybe Bytes` plus `fails with`, which is a point in Scribe's favour. The biggest real cost is the lack of zero-copy slices: idiomatic Go/Rust string processing cannot stay allocation-free.
